## Natural history notes

A small grass skipper characterized by dark brown wings with cloudy pale spots, a stout body, and a fast darting flight close to the ground. In Florida, the Clouded Skipper is common in lawns, fields, roadsides, gardens, pine flatwoods, forest edges, and other grassy open or semi-open habitats. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and live concealed in folded or tied grass blades, helping support birds, spiders, wasps, and other insect predators.
